docRequirement: plugins/loading.md#which-marketplaces-and-plugins-auto-update (was lines 425-442 of the retired discover-plugins page) binds us to a background auto-update mechanism: Claude Code "can automatically update marketplaces and their installed plugins in the background after startup", checking "after your session starts, with a random delay of up to ten minutes", then notifying the user to run `/reload-plugins`. Auto-update is a PER-MARKETPLACE toggle exposed in the plugin manager (Enable auto-update / Disable auto-update), whose default is polarity-dependent: "Official Anthropic marketplaces have auto-update enabled by default. Third-party and local development marketplaces have auto-update disabled by default." Administrators may force it on with `"autoUpdate": true` on an `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry; `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` turns everything off and `FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS=1` keeps plugin auto-updates alive alongside it.
current: No scheduled update path exists at any layer. (1) No per-marketplace flag is parsed: `deliveredRows()` at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-marketplace-entries.ts:384-403 projects an `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry to exactly `{at, name, source, ref}`, and `parseDeliveredMarketplaceEntryList` (same file, :334-381) builds `DeliveredMarketplaceEntryV1` (:104-111) from `name`/`source`/`refName` only — a policy carrying `"autoUpdate": true` is dropped silently, without even a recorded `ManagedDropSink` drop. (2) No persisted flag: `PluginMarketplaceRegistry` (packages/shared/src/plugins/store.ts:42-62) has `id/source/refName/sparsePaths/displayName/installedRoot/addedAt/lastUpgradedAt` and no autoUpdate. (3) No scheduler: the only catalog re-fetches are `PluginRegistrySource.upgrade()` (packages/shared/src/marketplace/registry-source.ts:834-883), reachable solely from the user-clicked RPC at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/marketplace.ts:364-382 wired to the button in apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/PluginsPage.tsx:752-762 (`RegistrySectionActions` offers Upgrade + Remove, no auto-update control), and `ensureBackgroundFetch()` (registry-source.ts:498-513) which is browse-triggered off `listItems()` (:434/:440), refreshes catalog metadata only, and never touches an installed bundle. `grep -a setInterval\|setTimeout` over packages/shared/src/marketplace, packages/shared/src/plugins and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap yields only fetch timeouts and the install-quota poll — no post-startup delayed job. (4) No plugin-bundle update: `PluginManagementServiceV2.update` (packages/shared/src/plugins/management-service-v2.ts:579-581) is `return this.repair(pluginKey, options)`, and `repairUnlocked` (:519-577) unconditionally re-stages the reconstructed source with no version comparison; it is reached only from the user-initiated `'repair' | 'update'` RPC action at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/plugins.ts:97-103. `MarketplaceService.refresh()` (packages/shared/src/marketplace/service.ts:171-173) just calls `PluginManagementServiceV2.refresh()` (:624-629), which prunes the store and returns status — it re-fetches nothing. (5) No update advertisement: `availableUpdateVersion` is declared at packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:683 and :747 and forwarded at :2201 and packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:403, but the production input provider never sets it (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:826-832 maps entries with `lifecycleState: 'ready'` and `listingId` only), so views.ts:443's `canUpdate: !!plugin.availableUpdateVersion` is structurally always false. (6) `grep -a` for `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` and `FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS` over packages/*/src and apps/*/src returns nothing; every `autoUpdate` hit in src is the Electron app updater (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts, logger.ts), a different subsystem.
divergence: The entire mechanism is absent, not misnamed and not narrowed. Six separable pieces are each missing: the per-marketplace `autoUpdate` boolean (unparsed from managed policy, unpersisted on the registry row, unexposed on the wire, absent from the UI); the polarity-dependent default (official-Anthropic-on / third-party-and-local-off — the fork has no concept of an 'official Anthropic marketplace' at all, so even the discriminator is missing); the post-startup check with a randomized delay of up to ten minutes; the installed-bundle update itself (`update()` is a pure alias of `repair()` — same-version re-stage, never a version comparison); the `/reload-plugins`-equivalent notification after an update lands; and both env kill-switches. The one adjacent behaviour that DOES exist — `ensureBackgroundFetch` re-cloning a stale catalog off the request path — is browse-triggered rather than scheduled and updates catalog metadata only, so it is not a narrower version of the documented behaviour but a different one. Because nothing ever sets `availableUpdateVersion`, even the manual path never tells a user an update exists.

Add `runScheduledAutoUpdate()` that iterates persisted registries, skips rows whose effective autoUpdate is false, calls the EXISTING `upgrade()` per row (:834-883 — it already handles allowlist refusal, single-flight, and the atomic cache swap), then asks plugin management to update the installed plugins whose `marketplaceId` matches. Stop aliasing repair (:579-581). `update()` must resolve the marketplace catalog's current version for the plugin's listing, compare it against `installed.version`, no-op when equal, and re-stage only on a newer version — otherwise the scheduler re-downloads and re-instances every bundle on every run. Publish the discovered newer version so `availableUpdateVersion` acquires a producer, and add a batch entry (e.g. `updateAllFromMarketplace(marketplaceId)`) the scheduler calls without an RPC round-trip. Keep `repair()` exactly as-is: it is the deliberate same-version re-stage and other callers rely on that.

blastRadius: Crosses a persistence boundary AND a wire boundary — both risk triggers in this repo. Persistence: `PluginMarketplaceRegistry` is serialized to marketplaces.json by MarketplaceRegistryStore.writeMarketplaceRegistries (registry-source.ts:140-144, backed by packages/shared/src/plugins/store.ts); the new field must be optional so an older file still loads and a rollback still reads the file. Wire: a new RPC channel plus a changed Safe registry-summary shape, enumerated by apps/electron/src/transport/__tests__/channel-map-parity.test.ts:89 and apps/electron/src/shared/__tests__/ipc-channels.test.ts:146. Managed policy: parseDeliveredMarketplaceEntryList is called from packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:1434-1449, covered by managed-policy.test.ts:433 and packages/shared/src/marketplace/__tests__/delivered-marketplace-policy.test.ts. Registry source: MarketplaceRegistryController is consumed by packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:303 and every handler in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/marketplace.ts; PluginRegistrySource has packages/shared/src/marketplace/__tests__/registry-source.test.ts, and `ensureBackgroundFetch` currently has NO covering test, so adding a scheduler beside it needs one. Changing `update()` to be version-aware alters the observable result of the existing user-facing 'update' RPC action (plugins.ts:97-103), which is covered by apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/__tests__/plugin-management-rows.test.ts:33, hooks/__tests__/useMarketplaceItems.test.ts:262 and marketplace-duplicate-rows.test.ts:173 — all three currently assert `canUpdate: false`, which stops being a tautology once a producer exists. Security-relevant: the scheduler downloads and activates code without a click, so `strictKnownMarketplaces` enforcement (registry-source.ts:388-393, already inside `upgrade()`) and the plugin trust gates must both stay on the scheduled path; a scheduled update must not be able to widen anything an interactive one cannot.
userImpact: Concrete and observable, in two places. A user who installs a plugin from a marketplace never learns a newer version exists: the plugin row's Update action is permanently unavailable because `canUpdate` is computed from a field nothing ever writes (views.ts:443 over resolver input storage-runtime.ts:826), so the only way to get a new version is to notice by hand, click the per-registry Upgrade button on the Plugins page to re-clone the catalog, then click the plugin's Repair — and the repair path re-stages the same version anyway unless the catalog moved. Plugins therefore sit at their install-time version indefinitely, including through upstream security fixes. Second, an administrator who writes `"autoUpdate": true` on an `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry from Claude's page gets nothing and is told nothing: the key is dropped before the managed-policy drop sink sees it, so it appears in neither config-doctor output nor the managed-drop report, and the marketplace behaves exactly as if the key were absent. There is no auto-update toggle anywhere in the plugin manager UI, so a user following the documented four-step path finds no such control.

Absence claims all made with `grep -a`. Two things the change list leaves open rather than decides, because the doc does not settle them and neither does the fork: (a) what counts as an 'official Anthropic marketplace' for the default polarity — this fork has no vendor-identity notion for a marketplace source at all, so the predicate has to be defined by an owner decision, and a conservative reading (default OFF for everything, honour only the explicit managed/UI toggle) is defensible and safer for a T-Bank deployment than inventing an anthropics/* allowlist; (b) whether the ten-minute randomized delay should be a literal port or a shorter desktop-appropriate window — the desktop shell has no per-session 'startup' the way a CLI session does. Not verified: whether `upgrade()`'s catalog re-clone is safe to run concurrently for N registries under the DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_FETCHES gate when nothing is browsing (the gate exists, the unattended path has never exercised it), and whether PluginInstallStager tolerates a staging run with no user present.
